summary: William Jones was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harrow School, Middle Temple, and University College, Oxford. In 1783, he became Chief Justice at the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, and founded The Asiatic Society in 1784.

William L. Ames is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Caltech and the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, and later held posts at John F. Kennedy University and other institutions.

William M. Bodiford is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned his Ph.D. from Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Davidson College and the University of Iowa before serving as Professor at UCLA from ~1992 to 2021.

William M. Gorvine works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Connecticut College and completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, where he studied under David Germano and others.

William Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at the University of Virginia and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

William Marshall Smart was an academic who studied at the University of Glasgow and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Cambridge from ~1919 to 1937 and at the University of Glasgow from ~1937 to 1959.

William Muir was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He studied at Kilmarnock Academy, the University of Edinburgh (~1834–1836), and Haileybury, later serving as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Edinburgh (~1885–1903).
William P. Chu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2006, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Price was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College (~1813–1830) and taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary (~1823–1830).

William R. Hutchison was a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at Oxford and Yale, taught at American University (~1959–1968), and spent the remainder of his career as a professor at Harvard University (~1968–2000).

William R. LaFleur was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago, he held faculty posts at Princeton, UCLA, and as E. Dale Saunders Professor at the University of Pennsylvania.

William Rainey Harper was a linguist and religious studies scholar educated at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale before becoming president and department head at the University of Chicago (1891–1906).

William Robertson was a historian who studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh (1733–1741). He served as Principal of the University of Edinburgh from 1762 and was a member of the Royal Society of Edinburgh.

William Roxburgh studied medicine at Edinburgh, Marischal College, and Aberdeen. He served in the Madras Medical Service, supervised Samalkot Garden from 1781, and became superintendent of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden in 1793.

William Shi-Yuan Wang is a linguist and sinologist who studied at Columbia and Michigan. He was a professor at UC Berkeley (1966–1994) and held posts at City University of Hong Kong, CUHK, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

William Stede was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He spent much of his academic career on the faculty at SOAS University of London and the University of London from ~1928 to 1949.

William Theodore de Bary was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religion. He studied at Columbia and Harvard, and served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia University from 1953 to 2017.

William Van Gordon is a researcher in religious and Buddhist studies. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (attested 2015).

William Ward was an Indology and religious studies figure who studied at Ewood Hall Academy under John Fawcett in 1797. He served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (~1800–1823) and co-founded Serampore College in 1818.

William Wilson Hunter was a historian and Indologist educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1861–1887) and became vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta in 1886.
